questions.q: Define meteorological drought and state the IMD's criterion for declaring it at the meteorological subdivision level.
questions.a: Meteorological drought occurs when seasonal rainfall is significantly below the long-term average; IMD declares it when rainfall departure is -26% to -50% (moderate) or >-50% (severe) from the normal for a subdivision. A wrong answer (e.g., confusing it with water shortage in dams) reveals the student cannot distinguish the atmospheric trigger from its downstream hydrological consequences.

questions.q: Explain why a region may experience hydrological drought even after the meteorological drought has ended.
questions.a: Hydrological drought lags because groundwater and reservoir recharge require sustained percolation over multiple seasons; aquifers and large dams have long memory. If a student says "hydrological drought ends with the first good rain," they misunderstand the storage inertia of surface and subsurface water bodies.

questions.q: Given a district with 600 mm annual normal rainfall, actual rainfall of 360 mm, and a 40% drop in reservoir storage, classify the drought types present and justify with numbers.
questions.a: Rainfall departure = (360-600)/600 × 100 = -40% → moderate meteorological drought (IMD: -26% to -50%). Reservoir storage drop of 40% indicates hydrological drought. Agricultural drought is inferred if soil moisture falls below wilting point for the dominant crop. A wrong classification (e.g., calling it severe meteorological drought) shows inability to apply IMD thresholds.

questions.q: Compare the drought vulnerability of the Marathwada region (Maharashtra) and the Thar Desert (Rajasthan) in terms of rainfall variability, groundwater dependence, and cropping pattern.
questions.a: Marathwada: high variability (CV >30%), heavy groundwater reliance for sugarcane, rainfed kharif crops → high agricultural drought risk. Thar: low mean rainfall (<250 mm), high variability, pastoralism + limited irrigation → chronic meteorological and hydrological drought. A student equating both as "low rainfall areas" misses the role of variability and human water use in shaping drought type.

questions.q: Evaluate the statement: "Providing free electricity for irrigation pumps is an effective drought mitigation strategy for peninsular India."
questions.a: Ineffective and counterproductive: it accelerates groundwater depletion, worsening hydrological drought, and encourages water-intensive crops in rain-shadow zones. A student endorsing it fails to link energy policy to aquifer sustainability and the distinction between meteorological trigger and anthropogenic amplification.

questions.q: Design a three-indicator early-warning dashboard for a district collector to monitor impending agricultural drought during the kharif season.
questions.a: 1) Weekly rainfall departure from normal (meteorological), 2) Reservoir live storage % of capacity (hydrological), 3) Satellite-derived soil moisture anomaly or NDVI deviation (agricultural). A poor answer listing only rainfall shows inability to integrate multi-source data for cross-sectoral drought typing.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Drought is a prolonged period of abnormally low precipitation leading to a shortage of water that adversely affects ecosystems, agriculture, and human activities; it is classified into ______ (deficit in rainfall), hydrological (deficit in surface/groundwater), and agricultural (deficit in soil moisture impacting crops) types, with India's most prone areas lying in the leeward side of the Western Ghats, Thar Desert, and rain-shadow regions of the Deccan Plateau.

Fill in the blank: Begin by asking students to recall the last time their city imposed water cuts or farmers in their state protested for crop insurance — this grounds the abstract concept in lived ______.
What is Drought? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Drought is a prolonged period of abnormally low precipitation leading to a shortage of water that adversely affects ecosystems, agriculture, and human activities; it is classified into meteorological (deficit in rainfall), hydrological (deficit in surface/groundwater), and agricultural (deficit in soil moisture impacting crops) types.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Drought?
questions.a: Students often treat "drought" as a single event defined only by low rainfall, ignoring that meteorological, hydrological, and agricultural droughts have different onset times, durations, and indicators — e.g., they assume a good monsoon immediately ends all drought types, not realizing reservoirs and aquifers need years to recover.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can distinguish between the three drought types using specific indicators (rainfall deficit, reservoir levels, soil moisture), identify India's drought-prone regions on a map with climatic justification, and explain the cascading progression from meteorological to hydrological to agricultural drought with a real-world Indian.
